Understanding prefixes and suffixes enhances English vocabulary. Prefixes alter word meanings, e.g., 'happy' to 'unhappy' (not happy). item.title: How Long is “A Country Mile”?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Educational content with explanations of idiomatic expressions and their origins, useful for understanding English usage.

The phrase 'a country mile' has a 300-year-old origin in the UK, meaning an approximate distance. Roads' unevenness can make it feel longer. Variants include Irish, Welsh, Scots, and Kentish miles, reflecting different measurement standards. It's often used in baseball to exaggerate distance.

Source: A Way with Words | Published: 2026-11-09 00:03 UTC
